modules.name: catalog
modules.description: Product listing, single-product lookup, and product creation. Lists products with an N+1 query pattern - one query for the product list, then one additional query per product to fetch its stock, instead of a single join.

modules.name: inventory
modules.description: Stock lookup and adjustment. adjust_stock reads the current quantity, computes the new value in Python, and writes it back as a separate statement - not atomic.

modules.name: cart
modules.description: Checkout and order lookup. checkout re-implements inventory's stock-decrement logic independently (reads products directly rather than going through catalog, and decrements inventory directly rather than calling inventory's adjust endpoint), and computes tax with a rate hardcoded only in this module.

modules.name: shared
modules.description: Not a domain module - infrastructure. Flask app factory and the sqlite connection helper every other module depends on. Owns the products/inventory/orders/order_items schema.

entry_points.description: GET /products - list, N+1 query against inventory per product.
POST /products - create product + seed its inventory row.
POST /cart/checkout - creates an order, duplicates inventory's decrement logic, hardcoded 8% tax, no idempotency key.

coupling_notes.description: cart.checkout duplicates inventory.adjust_stock's exact read-modify-write pattern instead of calling it - two independent implementations of the same non-atomic decrement, so a fix to one (e.g. adding locking) won't fix the other.
coupling_notes.evidence: ecommerce-app/cart/routes.py checkout() re-reads and re-writes inventory.stock_qty directly rather than calling inventory's adjust_stock route/logic.

coupling_notes.description: cart reads the products table directly for pricing instead of going through catalog's API - cart has to know products' schema, not just catalog's interface.
coupling_notes.evidence: ecommerce-app/cart/routes.py checkout(): 'SELECT price_cents FROM products WHERE id = ?' against the table catalog owns.

coupling_notes.description: order_items has real foreign keys into both orders and products, so cart's own tables can't be understood independently of catalog's schema.

deep_dive_notes: Churn is uninformative this run - the whole tree was introduced in a single commit, so every module shows churn_commits=1.
The tax rate (8%) is a module-level constant in cart/routes.py only; no other module references it, so if the business rate changes, whoever updates it has to know to look in cart specifically.

No idempotency key anywhere in checkout - retrying the same POST (e.g. a client timeout after a server-side success) creates a duplicate order and decrements inventory a second time for the same purchase.
No tests exist anywhere in this target. No input validation on any route (e.g. checkout doesn't validate qty is positive, adjust_stock doesn't validate the delta).
